Nema for Revenue operations

Keep revenue records and handoffs in sync.

Nema prepares focused reviews across marketing, sales, and customer success records using the definitions RevOps supplies. Owners can correct the exceptions without rebuilding the funnel by hand.

All teams ↗

Review the funnel using your definitions

Revenue teams lose confidence when lifecycle stages, owners, and dates mean different things across systems. Nema can apply the definitions RevOps maintains and prepare a queue of records that need attention.

Supply the required fields, stage rules, freshness windows, and system ownership. The output should explain exactly why each account or opportunity appears. RevOps decides whether the data, rule, or process needs to change.

Clean pipeline by exception

Start with open opportunities and a short set of checks: missing next step, overdue close date, absent owner, stage without required evidence, or conflicting account fields. Nema can group exceptions by seller and prepare a review in Slack.

Record changes should be explicit. Show the current value, proposed value, evidence, and owner before any write. Sellers and managers keep forecast categories and deal judgment outside this hygiene review.

Connect campaign and pipeline review

Give Nema an approved campaign report, attribution rules, and the matching funnel export. It can compare the supplied measures and identify gaps such as unmatched campaign members or inconsistent date windows.

The brief should state its attribution assumptions and source periods. Marketing and RevOps choose how to interpret the results, whether to investigate tracking, and whether to change the campaign plan.

Prepare account routing

For new accounts or leads, provide the team's territory, segment, ownership, and exception rules. Nema can collect missing firmographic details from approved records, show the rule that applies, and propose a destination.

RevOps reviews edge cases, duplicate candidates, and strategic-account exceptions. A proposed assignment should not silently overwrite an existing owner.

Improve handoffs across the customer lifecycle

Nema can compare sales commitments, commercial facts, onboarding needs, and renewal ownership to the handoff template. The result highlights missing owners, conflicting dates, and promises that need confirmation.

Sales, customer success, and RevOps accept the handoff together. This preserves the context while keeping each team responsible for its own records and commitments.

Start with read-only hygiene

Run one pipeline review without changing the CRM. Check the reason attached to each exception and tune the rules with record owners. Then choose a single field change set to review through the connected action. This creates a clear path from visibility to controlled correction.

Once owners correct the first queue, Nema can prepare the next review using the same lifecycle rules. The team sees whether exceptions are clearing, whether one field repeatedly fails at the same handoff, and whether the definition itself needs work.

For a monthly funnel review, RevOps can add agreed counts and conversion definitions to the same packet. Every number keeps its period and source, so marketing, sales, and customer success can discuss one shared view.

Questions from revenue operations teams

Can Nema work across CRM and marketing data?

Yes, when the required reads are available or you supply authorized exports. Align periods and account identifiers before comparing them.

Can Nema enforce our lifecycle definitions?

It can flag records that do not match approved rules and prepare corrections. RevOps owns the definitions and exceptions.

How are duplicates handled?

Nema can identify candidate duplicates using your criteria. A record owner reviews identity and approves any merge or correction.
